title: Terraform: GPU compute-pool autoscale abstraction and rolling upgrades
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a reusable Terraform module and migration plan for GPU compute pools in Private (VPC) deployments that unifies ASG and Karpenter autoscaling modes, provides safe rolling upgrades for GPU drivers and AMIs, and integrates liveness/driver health probes. Goal is to reduce past upgrade toil, standardize health checks across clusters, and provide a single config surface for platform teams.
acceptance_criteria: Single Terraform module (module path: modules/gpu-compute-pool) that can provision both ASG-backed and Karpenter-backed GPU pools via a 'provisioner_type' variable
Module supports a configurable rolling upgrade strategy with max_unavailable and graceful drain hooks for node-level eviction of pods and KV cache warmup for running inference workers
Built-in health checks: GPU driver readiness probe, nvidia-smi smoke test, and a node-level artifact check that triggers replacement when failing
E2E upgrade runbook documented and validated in a staging VPC: driver upgrade, AMI rotation, and a canary group flow
Automated Terraform plan + policy guard in CI (pre-apply) to prevent changes that would reduce GPU capacity below a safety threshold
Module exposes observability hooks (cloudwatch/prometheus labels) and outputs for Console to show pool capacity and last upgrade timestamp
technical_decision: Use a single module with 'provisioner_type' = ["asg", "karpenter"] to avoid drift between two separate modules
Adopt lifecycle hooks and SSM-based pre-drain signals for ASG; use Karpenter's disruption budget + taints for Karpenter flows
Perform driver upgrades via immutable AMI rotation where possible; fallback to in-place driver restart only when immutable builds are not available
Implement health checks as native node-level systemd service status + nvidia-smi return code to capture both driver and hardware failures
Expose a 'safety_min_available' variable and enforce with a Sentinel-like policy (implemented in CI) to block dangerous capacity changes
rollout_plan: 1) Merge module into infra-monorepo under modules/gpu-compute-pool and tag v0.1.0
2) Deploy to staging VPC with 'provisioner_type=asg' and run smoke tests (2 days), validate metrics and KV cache warming
3) Run an orchestrated AMI rotation in staging using canary subset (5% of nodes), monitor error rates for 24h
4) After staging signoff, schedule production rollout with automated gate checks and on-call rotation
5) For clusters currently using separate ASG/Karpenter modules, run a migration shim that imports state into the new module and performs a canary replacement
test_plan: Unit: terraform validate + terratest Golang suite for module variants (asg vs karpenter)
Integration: create small staging cluster (2 GPU nodes), simulate driver failure and assert automated replacement within defined SLA
Chaos: force node preemption and validate graceful drain and KV cache rehydration time <= 30s for p95 requests
Upgrade tests: AMI rotation simulation that exercises node cordon/drain, replica rebuild, and service-level error budgets
infra_changes: Add modules/gpu-compute-pool with entrypoints for asg and karpenter
Introduce SSM runbooks for pre-drain sanity checks and driver health scripts
CI policy: terraform plan checker to enforce safety_min_available and disallow destructive capacity reductions
Monitoring: add node-level exporter labels and a synthetic nvidia-smi probe to metrics
blockers: Waiting on immutable AMI build pipeline to publish GPU driver-enabled images with correct tagging (infra team ticket: INF-87). Also need approval from security for the SSM scripts in private clusters.
